text: Large language models (LLMs) are computer systems trained on vast amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. By analyzing patterns in this data, they learn to predict the next word in a sentence, which allows them to generate coherent responses. When you use an LLM, you give it a prompt—a question or instruction—and the quality of the answer often depends on how clear and specific that prompt is. This skill is called prompt engineering. LLMs can write essays, summarize information, and even code, but they have limits. They can make mistakes, repeat biases from their training data, and lack real understanding. So, while they are powerful tools, they should be used with careful human judgment.
